status: Proposals only; current definition and other audit artifacts unchanged.
review_method: Reviewed the 450 most frequent exact labels, focused candidate-name families and available targeted stored application snippets. This is not semantic review of all 42,936 names.
first_tranche: Foreshadowing/setup-payoff and dramatic irony are the strongest additional fixed-score evaluation candidates. Implement sparse structure/role concepts first for the remaining families.

proposals.meaning: Earlier details anticipate or enable later developments; setup is linked to payoff rather than merely recurring.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Twist frequency/impact measure revelations, and repeat_discovery measures affordance; neither identifies advance preparation. Narrative cohesion is a quality judgment.
proposals.proposed_change: Add sparse foreshadowing and consequential_setup_payoff concepts plus optional setup_event→payoff_event links. Evaluate storytelling.foreshadowing_intensity as a broad descriptor, independently of quality. Do not automatically add separate foreshadowing, Chekhov gun and payoff scores to similarity.
proposals.example_query: Intricate thrillers where small early details matter later
proposals.stored_context_summary: The stored FLOW entry explains an initially discarded buoy later helping the cat survive; Vortex links an early unattended stove to a later event. These establish a setup/payoff relation, not merely a surprise twist.
proposals.evidence_limit: Statistics count stored catalog IDs per exact label, not independently verified distinct works or observed searches. Stored snippets are title-specific applications, not canonical trope definitions; identity, application polarity and scope require validation.

proposals.meaning: The audience knows important facts that one or more characters do not.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Information withholding is a delay in information supplied to the viewer; dramatic irony can instead give the audience more information than a character. Unreliable narration is not required.
proposals.proposed_change: Add dramatic_irony/asymmetric_audience_knowledge as a narrative concept; evaluate a scoped storytelling.dramatic_irony_intensity descriptor if this repeatedly improves suspense/comedy search. Bind knowledge to audience and character where exact requests need it.
proposals.example_query: Thrillers where we know who the killer is while the characters do not
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Exit Smiling explanation describes a character wishing someone could play a role that the audience already knows she performed for him. Only one stored example was available in the targeted extract, so broader calibration remains outstanding.

proposals.meaning: A framing situation contains a narrated, written, performed or otherwise embedded story.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Meta-narrative and multiple viewpoints can occur without nested stories; flashbacks and anthology structure do not imply a narrative frame.
proposals.proposed_change: Add frame_narrative and embedded_story structure concepts, with parent_story/embedded_story and narrator relations. Avoid a universal nesting-complexity score.
proposals.example_query: Movies told as someone recounting their past; stories inside stories
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Sandakan No. 8 explanation describes a reporter eliciting an older woman’s story. King of Devil’s Island describes letters recasting events as a whaling story. These illustrate different frame/embedding uses.

proposals.meaning: The same event can be retold through conflicting accounts or revisited with new context.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Nonlinearity and multiple_viewpoints already cover broad structure. They do not establish that perspectives revisit the same event or contradict each other.
proposals.proposed_change: Add conflicting_retellings, repeated_event_new_perspective and retrospective_recontextualization as precise structure concepts. Preserve relations among accounts and the event; do not duplicate generic nonlinearity.
proposals.example_query: The same incident retold from conflicting perspectives
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Mexican source describes repeated, changing versions of a gun’s history; the My Tomorrow, Your Yesterday source describes revisiting earlier moments from another character’s perspective after a revelation.

proposals.meaning: Abrupt local tone changes and sustained tonal/genre evolution differ from mixed averages.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: The full V2 already has temporal_segments and explicitly distinguishes within-work from season-level change. This is an annotation/query extension, not a wholly absent data structure.
proposals.proposed_change: Add scoped abrupt_tonal_shift, sustained_darkening, sustained_lightening and genre_transition concepts; connect neighboring segments where evidence supports the transition. Defer any required global tonal_volatility score.
proposals.example_query: Comedies that turn into horror halfway through; sudden shifts between funny and disturbing
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Guest source describes a late transition from mystery-thriller to action-horror; the Super source describes humor diminishing as violence escalates; the Nowhere source describes repeated shifts among comedy, sex, sadness, violence and aliens.

proposals.meaning: Who is focal is distinct from who opposes whom, whether they are heroic, and whether opposition is a person, institution, environment or internal conflict.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Antihero is already broadly defined as departing from conventional heroic ethics/behavior. Morally ambiguous cast and character_emphasis do not establish villain protagonist or absence of a central villain.
proposals.proposed_change: Add villain_protagonist, decoy_protagonist and nonhuman_or_internal_opposition as role-bound concepts. Do not add a literal no_antagonist boolean: the stored No Antagonist example for FLOW explicitly calls the flood its antagonist. Record absence of a central villain only with assessed coverage.
proposals.example_query: Movies without a central villain; stories told from the villain’s perspective
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Letter explanation identifies the focal character as an adulterer and murderer. The FLOW explanation distinguishes obstacles and an impersonal flood from a single overarching villain. The Fargo example describes delayed focal-character introduction.

proposals.meaning: An active planner, a person swept along by events, a witness-narrator and a skilled practical worker are different character/story arrangements.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Child/female agency are existing dimensions, and intellectual_problem_solver covers reasoning. Practical competence, focality and general agency should not be collapsed into genius or action strength.
proposals.proposed_change: Add reactive_protagonist, supporting_narrator and practical_problem_solving concepts with role/scope. Consider replacing demographic-specific agency with a general agentive-character annotation plus role binding before adding another scalar.
proposals.example_query: Capable professionals doing their jobs; ordinary people swept into events
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Cast Away explanation describes trial-and-error survival engineering and rope calculations; the Spotlight explanation describes careful journalistic work. These are practical/problem-solving treatment, not a diagnosis of intellectual genius.

proposals.meaning: Moral decline, reform and changes of allegiance are related but not interchangeable.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: tropes.fall_from_grace explicitly includes losing moral standing; redemption and transformation_arc already exist. The new proposed corruption score concerns abuse of entrusted power, not every moral decline.
proposals.proposed_change: Use protagonist-bound moral_descent, moral_reform and allegiance_change subtypes only where useful. Reuse existing parent scores; do not add another broad moral_descent, corruption_arc or redemption score. Distinguish genuine reform from undercover deception or coerced alignment.
proposals.example_query: Protagonists who gradually become villains; enemies who genuinely reform
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Menace II Society explanation describes a child growing into an embraced criminal lifestyle. The To Kill a Mockingbird source describes a member of a lynch mob being shamed into changing his stance. These are directional arcs.

proposals.meaning: How a bond began and what commitment it involves are separate from current marriage/friendship/romance centrality.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Current seeds include fake_dating, friends_to_lovers and second_chance_romance; those do not imply arranged marriage, transactional marriage, childhood connection or enduring platonic partnership.
proposals.proposed_change: Add arranged_marriage, marriage_of_convenience, childhood_friends and enduring_platonic_partnership with character bindings. Do not infer sexual orientation from Heterosexual Life-Partners or explicit LGBTQ identity from shipping/ambiguous-relationship labels. Keep mutual romance versus interpretation separate.
proposals.example_query: Arranged marriages that become loving; lifelong platonic partners
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Tanna explanation says marriage is arranged by community custom and the character objects. The Animal Kingdom explanation describes a marriage proposed for legal parenthood. The Swap source frames an enduring bond as potentially becoming family rather than a romantic pairing.

proposals.meaning: Blackmail and framing someone for wrongdoing identify specific coercive/deceptive plot mechanisms.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Crime, coercive_relationship, institutional corruption and general deception do not establish these mechanisms. Do not treat them as synonymous with all betrayal or wrongful accusation.
proposals.proposed_change: Add blackmail and frame_up; model blackmailer, target, leverage and falsely accused roles when queries require specificity. Distinguish knowingly framing someone from an innocent mistaken accusation.
proposals.example_query: Blackmail thrillers; innocent people deliberately framed for crimes
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Exit Smiling source describes a threatened revelation of an earlier embezzlement frame-up, including the blackmailer, leverage and attempt to clear an accused person.

proposals.meaning: False leads and restricted access to suspects/escape routes are narrower than mystery membership.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Puzzle-box, information_withholding and locked_room are related. The current locked_room definition concerns an apparently inaccessible crime scene, not a whole group unable to leave or get help.
proposals.proposed_change: Add red_herring and closed_circle as precise concepts. Closed-circle can belong to survival/horror without a whodunit. Treat an averted expected payoff as a red-herring interpretation, not automatically failed writing.
proposals.example_query: Closed-circle mysteries where nobody can leave; mysteries full of false leads
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Abigail explanation describes surrendered phones and a locked-down mansion. The Three O’Clock High source describes multiple barriers preventing departure from school. The Highway to Hell source describes a warning apparently pointing at the wrong person.

proposals.meaning: Examining a convention’s consequences differs from parody; a recurring symbolic or musical idea differs from homage.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Parody/satire require comedy; self_reference is awareness of construction, and homage is tribute. Neither guarantees serious genre deconstruction. Symbolic/allegorical treatment is not automatically philosophical dialogue.
proposals.proposed_change: Add genre_deconstruction, reconstruction, allegory, symbolic_motif and leitmotif as treatment concepts where supported. Do not add one scalar for every symbolic object or evaluative profundity. Motif relations link occurrences to ideas/characters.
proposals.example_query: Serious deconstructions of superhero conventions; recurring symbolic imagery
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Split source explicitly examines how terrifying superhuman violence is to ordinary people. Current Rule of Symbolism examples only say nearly everything is symbolic; those excerpts are too vague for calibrated scoring. Leitmotif has inventory support but initially no reviewed snippet.

proposals.meaning: Episodes can reset consequential changes even while continuity references persist.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: formula_repetition concerns repeated plot patterns; episodic_independence concerns comprehension; serialized_dependence concerns prior knowledge. None alone establishes whether major changes persist.
proposals.proposed_change: Add episodic_status_quo_reset or persistent_consequences structure concept with episode/season scope. Avoid interpreting renewal status or sitcom format as proof. No new broad score is necessary before evidence/calibration.
proposals.example_query: Episodic shows where everything resets after each episode
proposals.stored_context_summary: The exact inventory label supports a candidate, but the initial stored-example extract did not include its application context. Keep this lower-evidence pending a representative source excerpt.

proposals.meaning: Character mortality, implausible survival and progressive cast attrition are different claims.
proposals.existing_coverage_boundary: Personal stakes, ending tragedy and gore do not establish who survives. Anyone Can Die is critical shorthand, not a probabilistic guarantee that each protagonist is equally vulnerable.
proposals.proposed_change: Add optional cast_attrition concept and character-specific outcome/arc relations under the already proposed event/role layer. Defer plot_armor or survival_predictability scalars; protect spoilers and preserve ambiguity. Never infer that a specific character dies from overall tragedy.
proposals.example_query: Survival horror where the group dwindles; does the main couple survive?
proposals.stored_context_summary: The Time-lapse source lists particular survivors and deaths, whereas the Das Boot Plot Armor source offers a detailed interpretive discussion of one survivor and wider losses. Different semantics require different representations.

conversion_contract_additions: Resolve canonical URL identity and aliases; exact names are not unique stable concepts.
Preserve media type, catalog ID, source page, scope, evidence and application status.
Detect played-straight, subverted, inverted, averted, defied, discussed and uncertain applications from prose before deriving content presence.
Do not use trope labels to infer an animal, occupation, disability, represented identity or on-screen event.
Treat role-bound outcomes and revelation details as spoilers.
Deduplicate actual work identities separately from distinct catalog IDs before interpreting prevalence.
